name: Fridge & utility room

dimensions.notes: Measured by the owners: space 116 cm wide × 231 cm (taken as floor-to-ceiling height — to confirm). 66 cm of wall between the back wall and the bathroom door opening. Washing machine 60 cm wide. Current fridge 54 cm wide × 142 cm high. Gap between fridge and right-hand wall: about 1 cm. The bathroom door is a pocket door inside the wall — it does not use any of the 116 cm.

orientation: Between the kitchen and the bathroom; the bathroom's sliding door opens off it

photos.caption: The space today: washing machine + fridge on the back wall, bathroom sliding door on the right, glass blocks above it
Bathroom door and the glass blocks above it, from this side — blocks to be plastered over

current.summary: Alcove 116 cm wide between the kitchen and the bathroom. On the back wall: Beko washing machine (60 cm) and a pink Candy fridge-freezer (54 cm wide, 142 cm high) — together 114 cm of the 116. The bathroom's pocket door (it slides inside the wall, so it takes nothing from the 116 cm) is in the right-hand wall, starting 66 cm from the back wall, with a row of glass blocks above it. Walls patched and unpainted; a socket and a switch sit on the back wall behind/above the appliances; one ceiling downlight. The washing machine's pipes and valves behind it are loose and need fixing into the wall.
issues: JOB 1 — Replace the fridge (current one not liked)
JOB 2 — Plaster over the glass blocks on this side
JOB 3 — Build wall cabinets above the fridge and washing machine so the space looks deliberate and organised
JOB 4 — Washing-machine pipes and water valves to be fixed into the wall properly

target.concept: DRAFT — a small fitted utility wall. Washing machine on the left under a timber worktop, a new tall fridge-freezer on the right, and one continuous run of cupboards across the full 116 cm up to the ceiling, with filler strips to the walls so it reads as built-in. Cupboard doors in the same green as the kitchen units; walls and the plastered-over glass blocks in the same warm white as the kitchen. Sockets moved to where they can be reached.

furniture.name: Top cupboards, full width
furniture.detail: 2 doors across 116 cm, from about 185 cm up to the 231 cm ceiling (≈45 cm high), ≈55 cm deep over the fridge side

furniture.name: Worktop over the washing machine
furniture.detail: At ≈90 cm, 60 cm wide — for the laundry basket / folding; open shelf or second cupboard between it and the top row

furniture.name: New fridge-freezer
furniture.detail: Freestanding, 54–55 cm wide (116 − 60 cm washer leaves 56 cm), up to ≈180 cm high under the top cupboards — much more capacity than the current 142 cm. Check the model's required side/top ventilation gap.

lighting.name: LED strip under the top cupboards

scope: Plaster over the glass blocks (this side)
Fix washing-machine supply and waste into the wall
Build and fit cupboards; fit new fridge

surfaces.prep: Glass will not hold plaster directly: fix plasterboard over, or mesh + bonding coat; joint to existing wall with scrim tape to prevent a crack line

Chase supply and waste into the wall. Fit a recessed washing-machine box (flush tap + trap in one wall box) so the machine can sit back to the wall and the isolating valve stays reachable — do NOT cement valves in where they cannot be turned off or replaced.
surfaces.notes: Move the socket(s) above worktop height so plugs are reachable; one socket for the fridge high on the right

surfaces.prep: Fill, sand, mist coat on new plaster

notes: Fridge needs ventilation: leave the gap the manufacturer asks for above and behind; do not box it in tight
